runners_data.name: Shadow Brigade
runners_data.note: Landed a recent 10f win on good ground and arrives 10 days fresh, giving her solid claims on form; by default the most likely pace-setter in this field despite naturally preferring to race from off the pace, so her chance is tempered by the discomfort of leading.|
runners_data.comment: Shadow Brigade bounced back to winning ways last time out and, rated 81, he heads this field on his merits; having run over today's going before, conditions hold no fears, and only a 138 lb burden gives any pause.

runners_data.name: Brighton View
runners_data.note: Won over 10f here at Yarmouth on good ground and has placed twice at the same course-and-distance combination, making her course form the standout angle in this field; a natural hold-up horse who should benefit from tracking whatever tempo Shadow Brigade sets.|
runners_data.comment: Brighton View shaped well when second last time out and brings a win three starts back into this contest, and his experience on today's going is a clear asset; the unplaced effort two starts back is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Mr Bollinger
runners_data.note: Comes here on the back of a win over 12f on good ground 10 days ago, suggesting the trip is no concern and he may even find 1m3½f on the sharp side; genuinely a deep hold-up horse by style, shifted one slot forward on the map only because the rear of the field is overcrowded — the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that slight positional compromise.|
runners_data.comment: Mr Bollinger arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a genuine threat off 127 lb; the chief concern is his trainer's dire recent strike-rate of just one winner from 22.

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Brigade is redistributed to the lead in this three-runner field, though her true style is hold-up; with no confirmed front-runner present, she is the most likely pace-setter by default rather than by instinct. The race will be run at a measured, sustainable tempo over 1m3½f on good-to-firm ground at Yarmouth — a flat, undemanding track that rarely generates false pace — meaning the gallop is unlikely to stretch the field or create a meaningful advantage for late closers. Brighton View and Mr Bollinger are both natural hold-up types, leaving this race critically short of genuine pace and creating conditions where whoever ends up in front dictates entirely on their own terms. This shape favours hold-up horses with the tactical acumen to time their run off a slow, controlled tempo — but with all three runners sharing that profile, the most influential factor will be which rider takes the initiative to bridge the gap at the right moment on the long Yarmouth home straight; the field contains more hold-up types than can all operate from their natural position, and Shadow Brigade — despite her redistribution to the lead — is the horse most likely to find herself in front by default.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo remains genuinely steady throughout and the race develops into a one-pace procession into the straight.
scenarios.body: Shadow Brigade drifts along in front at an uncontested crawl, but her redistribution from hold-up means she is not in her element leading and may lack the finishing kick when challenged; Brighton View and Mr Bollinger, tracking closely from their natural positions, are ideally placed to pounce off the bend.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Shadow Brigade Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Brigade, despite being a natural hold-up type, settles comfortably up front and kicks clear before rivals can organise a challenge.
scenarios.body: With such a small field and no one eager to press her, Shadow Brigade could dictate every yard and exploit any inertia among the two true hold-up horses who may leave their runs too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, No Pace
scenarios.trigger: If all three riders are reluctant to go on and the pace collapses into a dawdle, producing a sprint finish from a near-standing start.
scenarios.body: The long Yarmouth straight becomes a sprint finish, favouring the sharpest accelerator at this trip; Brighton View's course form (won over 10f here) gives her a meaningful edge in that scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mr Bollinger Outkicks Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Bollinger's strong recent win over 12f translates into superior stamina and he runs past a flagging leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mr Bollinger's latest form (1 over 12f good) shows he stays further than this trip well and could pick off tired rivals late, though his STYLE_FIT tag means this requires conditions to fall perfectly for him.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Brigade (Keenan) is a hold-up type on the lead by default — watch for her to be slow into stride or to drift off a very weak gallop, which could completely disrupt the race shape and hand an uncontested lead to whoever reacts quickest.

Brighton View has strong course-and-distance winning form at Yarmouth — if Ghiani positions her on the heels of Shadow Brigade from the outset, she has the tactical advantage of sitting exactly where she wants to be throughout.

With only three runners, the pace could evaporate to almost nothing — watch for a falsely slow opening half-mile that compresses the field and turns the race into a flat-out sprint from two furlongs out, a scenario that may not suit any of the confirmed hold-up types.

Mr Bollinger (Loughnane) is carrying the least weight at 127lbs and is trained by Michael Bell whose recent strike rate (1/22 over 14 days) is modest — monitor market confidence before the off as a significant market move would be notable in a field this small.

runners_data.name: Aspire To Glory
runners_data.note: Disappointing recent form (six runs without a win or place in similar going), and while Tom Marquand is a clear booking upgrade, this horse is a naturally prominent racer whose tactical options are squeezed by Oh So Audacious's presence; sim-going record of 2/15 with 0W0P does little to inspire confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Aspire To Glory at least brings distance and going experience to this contest, and his rating of 54 edges above his official mark — yet two sixth-place finishes last time out and two starts back are the high points of a lean recent spell, making consistency the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Nicely Curved
runners_data.note: Returned from 36 days off to a third-place finish last time and has twice placed at 8f on Good ground, giving her the most credible hold-up profile in the field; Jonny Peate has limited ammunition but this is arguably the most naturally suited closer on the day.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last three starts, Nicely Curved has experience of today's trip and going and arrives with a 36-day freshener to sharpen her up; the concern is she remains winless in recent starts and her official mark of 49 leaves little room for error.

runners_data.name: Oh So Audacious
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has raced 14 times on similar going with two wins and seven places — the form line is consistent if not dominant; Kaiya Fraser rides for a trainer in poor 14-day form (0/17) but the uncontested lead is a significant tactical gift that has to be respected at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Oh So Audacious arrives here just 11 days since her last outing, boasting experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 53 puts her right in the mix as a leading danger from stall one — though she's winless in her last five starts and that ninth last time out is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Busy campaign (only 4 days since last run) but Harry Davies is a sharp booking and this four-year-old has placed twice in six sim-going starts; races prominently by nature and that role is accessible here given the redistribution of the other prominent types, making it the most natural immediate challenger to the leader.
runners_data.comment: Valsharah arrives on the back of consecutive runner-up finishes two and three starts back, and our ratings rank him clear of these rivals; yet to score in recent starts, and a trainer in lean form is the one reservation worth noting.

runners_data.name: Caitlin G
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and a form string of 99754 leaves little to work with; the 3-year-old is carrying a lighter weight (129lbs) which helps marginally, but Good to Firm at Yarmouth over 7f has not suited, and Grace McEntee will need to produce something new to reverse this pattern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes no better than fourth, Caitlin G faces a stiff task as the bottom-ranked runner on our figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns fit on just 11 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Girls Allowed
runners_data.note: Longest break in the field at 53 days and a natural front-runner whose true role cannot be fulfilled with Oh So Audacious in the race; trainer in poor 14-day form (0/6) and three of the last five runs have been at the back of small fields, making a first-time competitive showing on fast ground hard to back with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of mid-pack and tail-end finishes, Girls Allowed faces a stiff ask here; the one comfort is she has run over today's trip and going before, and 53 days off may have freshened her up.

races.paceDynamic: Oh So Audacious is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five rivals in a 7f flat Yarmouth contest, is likely to get a clean lead and dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground. Aspire To Glory and Girls Allowed are both naturally prominent types but neither can fully express that role given the available space, with Oh So Audacious occupying the key position and the field too small to absorb multiple pace-pressing horses — both are effectively pushed into a midfield role against their instincts. Valsharah is the other genuine prominent-style runner and may try to sit just off the leader, creating a small group up front but not an especially fierce pace. This race shape — a single leader setting a measured tempo — classically favours horses who can sit close enough to strike at the furlong pole rather than deep closers, meaning the prominent-to-midfield profile with a strong cruising speed is best placed to capitalise. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate in those positions; Oh So Audacious is most likely to actually secure the lead, with Valsharah the only other runner with a realistic claim to sit directly behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Oh So Audacious sets an uncontested, honest but not scorching pace and holds off all challenges into the rising ground
scenarios.body: Oh So Audacious leads throughout on a track and trip combination where it has struck form before (14/15 sim-going runs, 2W7P), and a measured pace means no one can build the momentum to reel it in; horses close enough to the pace to pounce at the two-furlong pole are best served

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Cover
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough that the leader ties up in the final furlong, allowing a hold-up horse to arrive with a sustained run
scenarios.body: Nicely Curved has the most credible profile to deliver this, having placed twice at this trip and distance, and a slightly faster-than-expected pace could open the door for a late challenge from the rear; Caitlin G's fade tendency makes her a poor candidate despite also sitting back

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Aspire To Glory or Girls Allowed push forward early and force a contested pace that unravels the front-runner
scenarios.body: With both redistribution types feeling the pressure of not getting their natural position, early shuffling could elevate the pace and create a stronger tempo than expected, benefiting any horse with a high cruising speed who can slot into the resulting gaps; Valsharah's recent second-place finishes over similar ground give it the profile to capitalise

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Nothing Lands A Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a genuinely modest pace and horses flatline in the straight with no single runner able to assert
scenarios.body: A uniformly slow tempo on fast ground can compress the finish and produce a muddling result where class edges do not show, leaving the race open to a lower-rated runner who gets the perfect passage; Girls Allowed or Caitlin G could sneak into the money through positioning rather than merit

watchPoints.text: Oh So Audacious is the key pace setter — watch whether Aspire To Glory or Girls Allowed attempt to push forward at the start and challenge for the lead, because if they do the tempo lifts sharply and the entire race shape changes.
Valsharah ran only 4 days ago; watch for signs of a tired or flat performance in the final furlong, as a horse on a quick turnaround on fast ground can hit the wall late even if well-positioned.

Nicely Curved is 36 days off the track — watch the market move; if she shortens meaningfully it suggests the Hayley Burton team is happy with her readiness and the hold-up scenario becomes more credible.

Caitlin G is tagged as fading in the finish — watch her position at the 2f pole; if she is still travelling well at that point she may defy the tendency, but if she is already off the bridle she is unlikely to be a factor.

runners_data.comment: Daretobedifferent has distance and going experience to call on, and her third three starts back and win four starts back show she can perform at this level; rated highest of the six runners here, she arrives fresh on 23 days' rest. runners_data.name: Okiru
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides a hold-up three-year-old with a placed effort on Good to Firm at seven furlongs and a second from a recent run, though the form string (6U5724) lacks consistency; Archie Watson sends him out 24 days fresh with a hood (b) fitted, which may sharpen his focus in a race where he will need to pick up late.
runners_data.comment: Placed second two starts back and returning after 24 days, Okiru steps up with a 71 rating against an official mark of 64, and he has run over today's trip and going before — from stall one carrying 134 lb, he makes plenty of appeal despite being winless in his last six.

runners_data.name: Melting Snow
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's three-year-old wears a hood (p) and has been nudged into a midfield position on the map — the horse's true inclination is to race further back, which reduces confidence in any scenario that requires him to be handy; modest recent form (8564) and only four runs in comparable going yield no wins, though the drop to OR 62 keeps him competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a run of 4th, 6th, 5th and 8th hardly inspiring confidence, Melting Snow is hard to fancy at the foot of the market, though experience over today's trip and going, plus a race-fit 19-day gap, offer slim compensation.

runners_data.name: Guest House
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa booked for a horse who won over this exact trip (8f Good) and is placed four times in eight similar-going starts — genuine experience and a positive form string (3-1473) make him the most credible hold-up threat, though like the others he is mapped closer than his natural position suggests he will be.
runners_data.comment: Guest House arrives fit on a quick 10-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and a third last time out keeps him in good heart; the worry is that seventh two starts back hints at inconsistency he'll need to shake off.

runners_data.name: Bellini Spirit
runners_data.note: Longest absence in the field at 86 days and a career-low OR of 60; the John & Flint yard is in fair nick (3/8 over 14 days) but the form string (72-780) includes a 18th-place finish and inconsistent recent performances, while his natural hold-up style means he is unlikely to get an easy run from a midfield map position in a slowly-run race.
runners_data.comment: Bellini Spirit was second four starts back and has run over today's trip, giving her strong claims on fitness and experience once she returns from an 86-day absence — though she remains winless in recent starts and that layoff is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Esdaile
runners_data.note: James Tate's three-year-old drops to a career-low mark of OR 57 with a poor recent string (0650) and all four comparable runs showing a failure to finish in the frame; a natural hold-up horse operating out of his preferred position on the map, and the 12 days since last run is not a concern, but form does not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Esdaile faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a 12-day turnaround suggests she is fit, but that may be as far as the positives stretch.

races.paceDynamic: Daretobedifferent is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this six-runner mile handicap on Yarmouth's flat, straight track, and with no genuine rival to press him he is likely to control the tempo from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop — Good to Firm conditions will keep the race honest but not truly searching. All five of his rivals are genuine hold-up or prominent types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map because there is no second confirmed front runner to fill those slots; Melting Snow, Guest House, Bellini Spirit and Esdaile are the most notable examples of horses whose natural style is to race held up, but they are all mapped ahead of their true positions. With one uncontest leader and a field of closers who may struggle to get a true run of their natural race, this shape is a moderate-tempo affair that will see a compact group tracking Daretobedifferent before a sprint finish from around two furlongs out — a race that suits horses capable of travelling prominently or picking up quickly from just off the pace rather than deep hold-up types who need genuine early fractions to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Daretobedifferent dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the field strings out into a one-furlong dash.
scenarios.body: Daretobedifferent sets a sedate tempo from the front with no pressure, conserving energy, and the race becomes a flat-track sprint in the final two furlongs; horses who can travel close to the pace and quicken on Good to Firm ground benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Fire Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves deceptively strong or the field concertinas, allowing genuine hold-up horses to generate momentum from the rear.
scenarios.body: A bunched group tracking Daretobedifferent compresses into the final furlong and those with the cleanest late run find a gap at the right moment; Guest House and Okiru, both with prior winning form at this trip, are best positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Daretobedifferent is allowed a completely uncontested lead and the field fails to close the gap in the short Yarmouth straight.
scenarios.body: With no rivals willing to commit early and the leader perfectly balanced on fast ground, Daretobedifferent simply maintains his gallop and holds on; this rewards the sole front runner in a field that has no natural chaser to mount a sustained challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If pace is non-existent in the early stages and multiple hold-up horses get boxed in, producing a chaotic late sprint.
scenarios.body: With a field of true hold-up types all forced to race closer than ideal, the race devolves into a messy scramble from two furlongs out where winning is largely positional; Bellini Spirit, freshest on an 86-day break, and Esdaile, dropping to a career-low OR, represent value lottery tickets in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Guest House is the most dangerous horse in this race — prior win over the exact trip and going, Silvestre De Sousa in the saddle, and consistent Good-ground form; watch whether he can thread through from his hold-up position to challenge in the final furlong.

Daretobedifferent's redistribution to the lead is purely map-driven — he is a natural hold-up horse sent to the front by default, and if he fails to stride on comfortably early the entire pace dynamic collapses; watch his behaviour in the first two furlongs closely.

Okiru's hood fitting (b) is notable for a horse who has run inconsistently (6U5724 includes an unseated rider) — if the headgear has the desired sharpening effect and Tom Marquand gets a smooth passage, he could arrive late with more momentum than his odds suggest.

Bellini Spirit's 86-day layoff and step into a lower-grade race after his poor recent form is a flag for the market — the Flint yard's 14-day strike rate (3/8) is reasonable, so watch if he drifts or shortens in the final market move as a guide to stable confidence.

With five true hold-up horses in a six-runner field on a flat, straight mile, watch for a compressed finish where track position in the final two furlongs — not ability alone — determines the outcome; any horse that gets a clear run on the outside from two out is a major beneficiary.

races.paceDynamic: Cuban Girl is the only confirmed pace-setter in this field and will be allowed to slide into a comfortable, uncontested lead from the front, setting a sustainable gallop over 1m2f on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth's flat, undemanding track. All four remaining runners — The Ubermensch, Risen Again, Big Alex Walmsley, and Nuptown Girl — are natural hold-up types, meaning the race will likely string out behind Cuban Girl with a compact bunch tracking at varying distances. This shape — a lone leader, pedestrian fractions, and a bunch of closers who lack a true forcing pace — historically favours horses that can travel efficiently in the mid-to-rear group and produce a sustained finishing effort rather than a sharp late burst; The Ubermensch, with proven form at this trip and similar going, is the profile that fits best. This field holds more hold-up types than the map can naturally place, with Risen Again, Big Alex Walmsley, and Nuptown Girl all genuinely rear-of-field horses shown in midfield due to redistribution — of those three, Nuptown Girl's consistent recent form and Nuptown-to-front running style gives her the best chance of tracking closer than her natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Cuban Girl establishes an uncontested lead and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap before the home straight.
scenarios.body: Cuban Girl dictates every fraction unchallenged, the modest gallop plays to stamina and positional advantage, and any runner who travels close enough to make a clean challenge at the 2f pole benefits from not expending energy in traffic; The Ubermensch, proven over this trip on good ground and with a recent win, is best placed to make the smooth transition from tracker to winner.

scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Home

Good to Firm ground confirmed for this race — the going report is consistent across all Yarmouth races — which suits the majority of this field's historical profiles, though Risen Again's soft-ground bias in recent starts (SOF, STA appearances) could undermine his claims on this surface.

The main risk is he remains yet to win in recent starts, and that final hurdle may prove the stumbling block again.

runners_data.name: Antiphon
runners_data.note: Mike Murphy's 7yo is a confirmed hold-up horse who fades in finishes — flagged for doing so — and is placed in midfield on the map only because there are more closers than positions; his 0W3P at similar going masks a pattern of promising positions that rarely convert, and the 16-day break is neutral.
runners_data.comment: Antiphon has shown consistency at this level with thirds last time and four and five starts back, and he returns on a handy 16-day turnaround with distance and going experience to call on — the main concern is that he's winless in recent starts and must prove he can convert his placed efforts.

runners_data.name: Regal Guest
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa rides this 4yo whose natural style is hold-up, bumped to midfield by the redistribution of rear-of-field types; recent form over longer trips (7f-8f) raises a distance concern dropping to 5f, and an 0W record from 8 similar-going runs adds caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Regal Guest has at least shown going experience to call on, though consecutive mid-to-rear finishes and a rating of 48 suggest he faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Nad Alshiba Snow
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan rides this 4yo for Mike Murphy after a 62-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — wearing a tongue-tie; her history is exclusively at 5f on Artificial and Soft surfaces (0W1P), and the switch to Good To Firm represents an untested variable alongside her natural hold-up style that leaves her at a disadvantage today.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Nad Alshiba Snow faces a stiff ask here; 62 days off the track adds a fitness query, though she has run over today's trip and going before and at least has distance-and-conditions experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Surprise Again
runners_data.note: J.R. Jenkins' 4yo returns after 60 days and carries a "fades in finish" flag alongside a hold-up style — a difficult combination on a track where sustained pressure is required; form figures of 7007-8 and an 0W record from comparable going runs make it hard to make a case in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two seventh-place finishes and three unplaced efforts in recent form, Surprise Again is the clear outsider on our figures; 60 days off the track is a concern, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Papa Don't Preach is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 5f handicap and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to push her — she can slide into a comfortable lead and control every fraction on the Yarmouth straight. The going report confirms Good To Firm conditions throughout the card, a surface entirely within her comfort zone given her recent Goodwood and similar-ground form. With the remainder of the field comprised of hold-up types — Antiphon, Regal Guest, Nad Alshiba Snow, Surprise Again, Dragon God, and Mart — none of whom naturally want to make the running, the tempo will be dictated by one horse alone, and those behind will be chasing a moving target from the outset on a track that offers no bend to compress gaps. This race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent and front-running profiles; hold-up horses will need an unusually strong gallop to close, and with only one horse supplying that gallop, they are unlikely to get it. Several runners — Regal Guest, Antiphon, Surprise Again, and Nad Alshiba Snow — are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield by redistribution, and of those most likely to push closer than natural, Dragon God and Mart have the most relevant recent form to compete for early positions just off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Papa Don't Preach hacks up front unchallenged and sets a moderate-to-fair gallop that the closers cannot reel in.
scenarios.body: Papa Don't Preach bowls along in front on this flat, straight 5f, controlling the race entirely; at Good To Firm the pace is unlikely to be strong enough for hold-up horses to close on a relatively modest mark of OR 55. Horses that can travel just off the leader — Dragon God or Mart if they creep forward — are best placed to challenge late, but the leader's comfort and jockey advantage (Billy Loughnane) make her hard to pass.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Papa Don't Preach sets a stronger gallop than expected and ties herself up in the final furlong, opening a window for a finisher.
scenarios.body: A faster early pace would compress the field and give the hold-up horses — who are numerous but largely racing out of role here — a realistic chance of closing; Dragon God's recent 3rd and 2nd at 5f on Good ground makes him the best-credentialled to exploit late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the race turns into a flat-out sprint from the 2f pole with few separating until late.
scenarios.body: A falsely run affair over 5f can produce a wall of runners hitting the line together; in that scramble, horses like Dragon God with the highest TopSpeed credentials and Tom Marquand's tactical awareness could benefit from a tighter, more compressed finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the favourite stumbles early or is checked at the start, handing an unexpected advantage to a horse that secures an uncontested prominent position.
scenarios.body: Mart or Regal Guest could inherit a lead or prominent slot they would not normally occupy; Silvestre De Sousa on Regal Guest has the experience to exploit positional chaos immediately.

watchPoints.text: Papa Don't Preach's start is critical — if Billy Loughnane gets a clean break she controls this race unchallenged; watch for any slow break that would allow Dragon God or Mart to steal a prominent position and fundamentally alter the shape.

Dragon God represents the principal tactical threat from off the pace — Tom Marquand will be watching for a gap inside the final furlong, and if Papa Don't Preach has used herself setting even a modest pace, this is the horse most likely to mow her down.

With four genuine hold-up horses (Antiphon, Regal Guest, Nad Alshiba Snow, Surprise Again) all competing for the same closing ground on a straight 5f, there is significant risk of traffic problems in the final two furlongs — watch for crowding around the 1f marker.

Nad Alshiba Snow and Surprise Again both return from 60+ day breaks; monitor both in the paddock for condition and watch whether either travels freely in the early stages, as a rusty display from either would remove two of the few pace-pressing options from the equation entirely.
